description: HOLDOUT test architecture (not used during development). Manually curated STRIDE ground truth for a mobile banking backend. Flows are well-secured and the database is encrypted and audited; the real risk lives in configuration: no device binding or certificate pinning at the gateway, transaction authorization that only checks authentication (no step-up/transaction signing), and a fraud-detection service that is switched off. Hard threats require mobile/financial security knowledge and config reasoning; the deterministic baseline cannot find them. easy = exactly what the attribute-based deterministic baseline detects.

threats.description: The internet-exposed gateway can be targeted by clients impersonating legitimate users or replaying captured tokens.
threats.mitigation: Validate tokens on every request and bind sessions to a verified identity.

threats.description: Without certificate pinning, a man-in-the-middle on a compromised device or network can intercept and modify banking traffic.
threats.mitigation: Require certificate pinning in the app and reject unpinned connections.

threats.description: With no device binding, a stolen token or session can be replayed from any device, letting an attacker act as the victim.
threats.mitigation: Bind sessions/tokens to an attested device identity and detect device changes.

threats.description: The app stores sensitive data on the device, which can be extracted on a lost, stolen, or jailbroken device.
threats.mitigation: Minimize on-device data, use secure storage/keystore, and detect compromised devices.

threats.description: Transactions are authorized by authentication alone with no step-up auth, so a hijacked session can initiate high-value transfers the user never approved.
threats.mitigation: Require transaction signing / step-up authentication for sensitive operations.

threats.description: Without per-transaction signing or strong authorization evidence, users can dispute transactions and the bank cannot prove intent.
The service handles sensitive account and transaction data that could be exposed through logging or over-broad responses.
threats.mitigation: Minimize returned fields and redact sensitive data in logs.

threats.description: Fraud detection is disabled, so fraudulent transactions pass unchecked — a critical compensating control is absent.
threats.mitigation: Enable fraud detection and fail closed for high-risk transactions.

threats.description: The accounts database stores highly sensitive financial data that could be exposed if access controls fail.
threats.mitigation: Keep encryption at rest, restrict access, and monitor queries (already partly configured).
